equity_bridge.note: FY2026 AR: restructuring and severance costs of US$12.9m recognised on the June 2026 closure announcement, largely unpaid at balance date. Estimate; pre-tax.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (1.5%) diverges by more than 30% from the revenue 5-year CAGR (5.4%). Book equity is suppressed by dividends, US$120m+ of buy-backs since FY2024 and the US$73.8m FY2026 impairment, so it understates business growth; the revenue 5-year figure is flattered by the Holman acquisition (FY2024). The base growth path is anchored to FY2027 guidance (mid-to-high single digit) fading to 3%, not to the equity CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: All CAGRs on USD figures, FY2021 (restated to USD) and FY2023 to FY2026. EPS CAGRs use Adjusted EPS of US16.5c for FY2026 because statutory EPS of US0.8c is after US$103.3m of post-tax one-offs (statutory: -64% 3-year, -46% 5-year). FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC): FY2021 164.3, FY2023 201.9, FY2026 213.0. SBC is ~0.6% of revenue and has grown in line with it, so owner and reported FCF CAGRs are effectively the same.

scenario_narratives.base: Standalone RWC if the scheme fails. FY2027 lands on guidance (sales up ~6%, Adjusted EBITDA margin ~18.5%) with US and UK repair-and-remodel demand still soft. From FY2028 the margin rebuilds to 20.5% on three identified items rather than a market recovery: tariff cost falling from US$25-30m to US$5-7m as Mexico and Poland capacity comes on, Poland ramp costs dropping out of EMEA, and ~US$9m a year saved from exiting Melbourne brass manufacturing. It does not get back to the 21-22% of FY2023-25 because copper costs and big-box pricing pressure persist. Growth fades from 6% to 3% as SharkBite PEX Press, Max and continental Europe add modestly to a GDP-like replacement market.
scenario_narratives.bull: US housing turnover and remodel activity recover from 2027 as rates ease, and RWC's operating leverage works in reverse of FY2026: Americas volumes rebuild, the unified SharkBite push/press/expansion system and the stainless range take share, and John Guest scales through continental DIY retail. Sales grow 7-8% for two years and the margin returns to 22.5%, the level the business earned in FY2023-24 before tariffs and destocking. This is the case in which US$3.38 looks like Brookfield buying at the bottom of the cycle.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY2026 margin step-down is structural rather than cyclical. US remodel demand stays flat, Section 232 tariffs and copper costs are only partly recovered in price, and ageing push-to-connect patents let Quick Fitting and private label take shelf space at Lowe's and the wholesalers, so the margin settles at 17.5% and sales barely grow for two years. A second round of footprint write-downs, as in APAC, is consistent with this path. In this case even the pre-bid share price was too high and the scheme consideration is a clear gift.

deal_analysis.status: Binding Scheme Implementation Deed with Brookfield Capital Partners signed 2026-09-16; board unanimously recommends, subject to no superior proposal and the independent expert; go-shop closed 2026-10-15 with no rival bid; scheme booklet lodged 2026-10-30; Second Court Hearing expected 2026-12-07; completion targeted Q1 2027. Dividend and buy-back suspended; any dividend paid reduces the consideration.
deal_analysis.consideration_currency_caveat: UNVERIFIED which currency is fixed. The scheme booklet is not in the research folder; the Analysis describes the price as US$3.38 (A$4.75 equivalent, AUDUSD ~0.7116 at signing) and 'payable in A$ or US$'. AUDUSD is now 0.6774. If the US$3.38 is fixed and converted at completion, the consideration is worth ~A$4.99 today and the price at inputs.price_as_of sits ~7.4% below it. If A$4.75 is fixed, the spread is ~2.8%. The 52-week high of A$4.79 (above A$4.75) is weak evidence for a US$-fixed price, but a 7% gross spread on a recommended, uncontested cash scheme two to four months from completion would be unusually wide, so the terms should be read off the scheme booklet before acting on the spread.
deal_analysis.implied_deal_multiples: At US$3.38 x 752.0m diluted shares = US$2,542m equity; plus US$243m net debt = US$2,785m EV ex-leases (US$2,893m with lease liabilities). That is 11.5x FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA ex-leases (12.7x after deducting lease cash from EBITDA), ~20.3x FY2026 Adjusted NPAT, and ~19-20x the model's FY2027 unlevered owner FCF.
deal_analysis.pre_bid_reference: The consideration was stated as a ~43% premium to the six-month VWAP, implying an undisturbed price of roughly A$3.32; the last weekly close before the 18 August 2026 announcement was A$3.67.
deal_analysis.break_price_basis: If the scheme fails the shares fall toward standalone value. Two estimates: the market's own undisturbed range of A$3.3-3.7, and this model's standalone weighted IV (probability_weighted.weighted_iv, about US$2.81 at this build), which sits above the pre-bid range and below the consideration. A$3.60 is used as the break price in the expected-value line because a broken deal usually trades back to the undisturbed price first.
deal_analysis.completion_probability_judgment: ~90%. For: binding deed, cash, unanimous board recommendation, go-shop produced no rival, court has ordered the meeting. Against: 75%-by-value and majority-by-number votes with AustralianSuper and Aware Super holding ~20.2% between them; court approval; any outstanding regulatory or foreign-investment condition (status not confirmed from the materials in the folder).

expected_value.reading: 0.90 x consideration + 0.10 x A$3.60. On an A$4.75-fixed reading the market price equals the expected value almost exactly, i.e. the shares are priced as a ~90% deal with no excess return; on a US$-fixed reading the market would be leaving ~5% on the table, which is why the consideration currency must be confirmed from the scheme booklet. Spread percentages are measured from the market price at inputs.price_as_of.

valuation_philosophy.summary: RWC is a deal-arbitrage situation, not a long-run fundamental one. A binding, board-recommended, uncontested cash scheme from Brookfield at US$3.38 per share is the dominant driver of the share price until it completes (targeted Q1 2027) or fails. The DCF here answers two narrower questions: is US$3.38 a fair price, and where do the shares go if the scheme breaks. On the house standalone build (USD flows at a 9% WACC, Adjusted EBITDA margin recovering to 20.5% from a depressed 18.5%), the base case (about US$2.93) and the probability-weighted value (about US$2.81) sit roughly 13-17% BELOW the consideration but above the undisturbed pre-bid price of A$3.3-3.7; the bear case, in which the FY2026 margin is the new normal, is well below even the pre-bid price; and only the bull case (a US housing recovery plus a full return to FY2023-24 margins, about US$3.64) is worth more than US$3.38, and by less than 10%. So the offer pays for most of a reasonable recovery, which is consistent with a go-shop that drew no competing bid, and the DCF gives no basis for holding out for more. The expected outcome for a holder is the consideration, not the DCF. The payoff is asymmetric: upside is capped at the consideration (about 3% if A$4.75 is the fixed amount, more if US$3.38 is fixed and converted at today's weaker AUD), while a failed scheme means a fall of roughly 10-25% toward the standalone value and the pre-bid price. weighted_iv below current_price therefore does not signal overvaluation in the usual sense; it measures the downside if the deal breaks. This is not a position for a 15% hurdle investor: the hurdle entry price is far below the market, and the only return on offer is the deal spread.
key_risks_to_valuation: Scheme failure: the 75% vote (AustralianSuper and Aware Super hold ~20.2%), the Second Court Hearing on 2026-12-07, or an unconfirmed regulatory condition. The shares would re-anchor to standalone value, roughly the pre-bid A$3.3-3.7.

Consideration currency: it is not verified from the scheme booklet whether US$3.38 or A$4.75 is the fixed amount. With AUDUSD down ~5% since signing the two differ by ~A$0.24 a share, which is the difference between a ~3% and a ~7% spread.

Margin normalisation: the whole spread between bear and bull is whether 18.5% Adjusted EBITDA margin is a trough (tariffs, copper, Poland ramp, destocking) or a new level (generic push-to-connect competition, big-box bargaining power). Each 1pt of terminal margin is worth roughly US$0.20-0.25 a share.
Cash tax: FY2026 cash tax of US$22.8m is flattered by ~US$15.5m a year of goodwill tax amortisation that runs off; the model ramps the rate to 25%.
FX: USD flows valued against an AUD quote. The AUD values move one-for-one with AUDUSD, and refresh_price does not update inputs.fx_rate.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 2.86-4.79 AUD. AUDUSD from Yahoo AUDUSD=X, 2026-11-14.
data_sources.financials: RWC FY2026 Annual Report (30 June 2026; USD): cash flow statement, net debt note 13, lease reconciliation, share capital and EPS notes, one-off reconciliation, FY2027 outlook assumptions. History from RWC.AX_Metrics.csv (USD from FY2021 restated; AUD before).
data_sources.qualitative: RWC.AX_Analysis.json (2026-11-15) for the scheme timeline, guidance, and bull/bear axes. The scheme booklet itself is not in the research folder.

inputs.share_count_basis: 748.039m ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (FY2026 AR share-capital note, after 25.5m bought back and cancelled in the year) plus 4.0m share options from the diluted-EPS table. Unvested performance rights are satisfied from treasury/trust shares already inside the issued count. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. The Metrics CSV figure of 763.3m is the FY2026 weighted average and is stale after the H2 buy-back.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report share-based payment expense note (US$7,901k; FY2025 US$7,370k). No net-share-settlement tax line; rights are settled from on-market treasury purchases (US$3.4m in FY2026).
inputs.fx_note: Flows and statements in USD (reporting currency since H1 FY2022); ASX quote in AUD. USD->AUD 1.4762 = 1 / 0.6774 AUDUSD (Yahoo AUDUSD=X, 2026-11-14). No dual listing for a parity check; direction check instead: US$3.38 x 1.4762 = A$4.99, and the deed's own stated equivalence of US$3.38 = A$4.75 implies AUDUSD 0.7116, which matches the mid-September 2026 spot (0.714-0.718). AUD has since weakened ~5%, which matters for the deal spread (see deal_analysis). refresh_price does not move this rate.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T05:10:11Z regular ASX close (Yahoo Finance chart API)
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.0%, built in USD because the flows are USD-reported and ~60% US-sourced: US 10-year ~4.3% risk-free, 5.0% ERP, beta ~1.1 for a housing-linked building-products manufacturer gives ~9.8% cost of equity; pre-tax debt cost 4.2% (FY2026 weighted average funding cost, 92% fixed), ~10% debt weight at market values. One WACC for all three scenarios: cyclicality, tariffs and competitive risk are carried in the scenario flows, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Adjusted EBITDA is post-IFRS 16, so the full FY2026 lease payment of US$23.2m (US$18.6m principal + US$4.5m interest, cash-flow statement) is charged as lease_cost_pct_path at ~1.75% of revenue, lease liabilities of US$107.9m are EXCLUDED from net debt (net debt is the company's own US$243.4m, borrowings at face less cash), and da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (US$72.0m less US$18.8m ROU = US$53.2m in FY2026).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF via the Drivers route, with the non-US/cyclical adaptations (USD flows vs AUD quote, leases, negative working-capital capture). ROUTING CAVEAT: RWC is under a binding Brookfield scheme at US$3.38 cash per share. The dcf-methods routing table sends a live scheme to deal-completes vs deal-breaks weighting; this build was requested as a standalone owner-FCF DCF, so the three scenarios and weighted_iv are the STANDALONE fundamental value (what the shares are worth if the scheme fails, and the yardstick for whether US$3.38 is a fair price), and the deal-completes/deal-breaks expected value is carried separately in the top-level deal_analysis block. Do not read weighted_iv vs current_price as an upside figure while the scheme is live: the price is anchored to the deal consideration. OWNER FCF: reported_fcf is OCF less capex from the Metrics CSV (US$240.7m - US$19.7m); this filer books interest paid (US$16.6m) and lease payments (US$23.2m) in financing, so reported FCF is unlevered and pre-lease, and FY2026 also benefited from a US$20.5m payables inflow and unusually low cash tax (US$22.8m vs US$38-42m in FY2022-25). The forward build therefore starts from components, not from last_fcf; year-1 unlevered owner FCF is ~US$143m. Interest income (US$1.4m) is not stripped because the company is in net debt. BUYBACKS: US$62.4m in FY2026 (repurchaser; flat count is funded), suspended with the dividend on 18 August 2026 pending the scheme. ONE-OFFS: FY2026 statutory EBITDA of US$131.6m carries US$110.5m of one-off items (US$73.8m APAC intangible impairment; US$37.7m APAC manufacturing restructure, of which ~US$25.7m is non-cash write-downs of inventory, PP&E and right-of-use assets and ~US$12.9m is cash severance and exit cost); the margin path is anchored to Adjusted EBITDA of US$242.1m (18.5%) and the unpaid cash restructuring is deducted once in the equity bridge.

base.rationale: Year 1 is FY2027 guidance: mid-to-high single-digit sales growth, Adjusted EBITDA margin broadly flat at ~18.5%, capex US$25-30m, D&A US$64-68m (less ~US$18.5m ROU depreciation), adjusted tax rate 18-21%. Margin recovers to 20.5% (below the 21-22% of FY2023-25) as Poland ramp costs recede, FY2027 tariff cost falls to US$5-7m from US$25-30m, and the ~US$9m/yr APAC saving arrives from FY2028. Capex normalises from a guided 2.0% to 3.0% of revenue (FY2022-25 averaged ~3.5%). Cash tax ramps from 19% to 25% as the US$15.5m/yr goodwill tax-amortisation benefit runs off. Working capital is negative capture: receivables + inventory less payables is ~25% of revenue.

entry_price.method: House default: terminal value rebuilt at the 15% hurdle. Not adjusted for the scheme. While the scheme is live the hurdle entry price is academic: a holder is paid the deal consideration within months if it completes, and the relevant return is the annualised deal spread in deal_analysis.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Standalone weights, conditional on the scheme NOT completing; they are not deal probabilities (those are in deal_analysis). Bear 25%, above the 15% house default: adjusted EBITDA fell 12.8% in FY2026, management guides no end-market improvement, and tariff and copper exposure is open-ended. Base 50%: it needs only guided FY2027 delivery plus three already-announced cost items. Bull 25%, below the 35% default: it needs a US housing recovery, share gains from new platforms and a full margin round-trip together, and a board that judged that outcome likely would not have unanimously recommended US$3.38 after a go-shop that drew no rival.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
